BREAKING: @Google just dropped Gemini 4 Carbon. It’s a much better coder than Argon—but I’m probably keeping Argon for writing. We’ve been testing it at @every across coding, writing, design, and knowledge work. It can work for hours on an ambitious project, but it doesn’t always know when to stop. Here’s your day-zero vibe check: • Coding: On one run of our Senior Engineer benchmark, Carbon scored 44%, versus Argon’s 21%. A big improvement, though still middle of the pack. In a separate test, @hammer_mt gave it a backlog to work through. It identified 6 tasks as ready, then did 15—including work someone else was already doing. He stopped it after almost 4.5 hours. • Big builds: @RandyCounsman gave it 3D scans of our podcast studio and an equipment list. In one attempt, it built a browser-based model accurate enough to check whether new gear would fit without getting into the shot. He estimates Carbon also wrote about 95% of a big update to Everycut, our internal video editor. • Code quality: @kieranklaassen values its tests and documentation on large projects, including its record of approaches it considered and rejected. Fable remains his first choice, but Carbon has earned a place alongside it. The catch: It can produce huge files where Fable keeps things more modular. • Audio and video: Randy found it caught audio editing issues other models missed. Kieran handed it a recorded meeting and asked for shorts. It came back with 6 titled clips. • Design: @jackcheng got a hyperrealistic ginkgo-leaf app icon with details other models struggle with. Objects and 3D scenes look better than Argon’s. Interfaces split the team: Jack and Randy kept getting boxes within boxes, while @TylerNishida liked its ideas for new interfaces. Kieran says giving it design guidance makes a big difference. • Writing: Our editorial benchmark put Carbon and Argon about even. If you like Argon, you’ll probably like Carbon. But Carbon costs more, and I haven’t seen enough improvement to justify switching. My Reach Test: 🟨 I’ll use it sometimes. Give it one big job with a clear finish line, and review what comes back. It’s also worth trying as a second opinion, especially on audio and video. Full vibe check coming soon: https://t.co/Ch2pNl9Po5
